metrics.definition: Probability that a random hidden positive is ranked above a random negative (area under the ROC curve); ties count half.
metrics.label: AUROC
metrics.reading: Separation over the whole ranking. Insensitive to how rare positives are, so a high AUROC can coexist with a poor top of the list -- read it with AUPRC.

metrics.chance: the prevalence (share of positives among everything ranked)
metrics.definition: Average precision: the mean, over the hidden positives, of the precision of the ranking down to that positive (area under the precision-recall curve).
metrics.label: AUPRC
metrics.reading: How clean the top of the ranking is. Its chance level is the prevalence, so compare it with that (AUPRC lift), never with 0.5.

metrics.definition: AUPRC divided by the prevalence, its value for a random ordering.
metrics.label: AUPRC lift
metrics.reading: How many times better than a random ordering the ranking is, where it matters. Comparable across tests with different prevalences, unlike AUPRC itself.

metrics.chance: not applicable (a property of the test)
metrics.definition: Hidden positives divided by everything ranked.
metrics.label: Prevalence
metrics.reading: The chance level of AUPRC and of precision at any depth; context for every other number.

metrics.definition: AUROC restricted to false-positive rates up to 10%, rescaled (McClish) so 0.5 is chance and 1 perfect.
metrics.label: Partial AUROC (FPR <= 10%)
metrics.reading: Separation in the part of the ranking anyone would act on; what matters for screening.

metrics.definition: Precision among the top R items, where R is the number of hidden positives. Equal to recall at that depth.
metrics.label: R-precision
metrics.reading: If you took as many candidates as there are true positives, the share that would be right.

metrics.definition: Share of positives among the top 1% of the ranking (at least one item).
metrics.label: Precision @ top 1%
metrics.reading: How good the very first candidates are -- the list anyone would test first.

metrics.definition: Precision at the top 1% divided by the prevalence.
metrics.label: Enrichment @ top 1%
metrics.reading: How many times more positives the first 1% holds than a random 1% would.

metrics.definition: Share of all hidden positives found in the top 10% of the ranking.
metrics.label: Recall @ top 10%
metrics.reading: How much of the answer a short list contains.

metrics.definition: The highest F1 (harmonic mean of precision and recall) over every cut-off of the ranking.
metrics.label: Best F1
metrics.reading: The best single-threshold trade-off the ranking allows; optimistic, since the cut-off is chosen on the answer.

metrics.chance: depends on prevalence; low when positives are rare
metrics.definition: Normalised discounted cumulative gain: positives count 1 / log2(rank + 1), divided by the value of a perfect ranking.
metrics.label: nDCG
metrics.reading: A whole-ranking score that weights the top most, smoothly rather than at one cut-off.
